articles.title: Ranking the 15 Weirdest Sports Injuries of All Time
articles.summary: Injuries are an unavoidable part of being a professional athlete, but some are a lot more difficult to explain than others.
articles.body:
Injuries are an unavoidable part of being a professional athlete, but some are a lot more difficult to explain than others.

Over the years, there have been some truly weird injuries suffered by some high-profile figures in the sporting world.

Sometimes those injuries are self-inflicted, like Jason Pierre-Paul's fireworks incident or Bill Gramatica's torn ACL celebrating a field goal.

Other times, they are a case of extreme bad luck, like the Norwegian soccer star who hurt himself while running from a charging moose on a jog.

With credit given to the truly unusual and unlikely, we've selected the 15 weirdest sports injuries of all time and provided our definitive ranking.

The Headline: Rockies' Rookie Falls Hauling Todd Helton's Venison

The Details: There is a long list of athletes injuring themselves by falling down, so rather than occupying a significant portion of this list with varying examples, we've simply selected the weirdest.

Clint Barmes was having a terrific rookie season for the Colorado Rockies in 2005. Veteran Todd Helton had him and fellow rookie Brad Hawpe over to his ranch for dinner. The Hall of Famer sent Barmes home with a raw slab of the venison they had eaten for dinner.

On his way up the stairs upon returning home while hauling the meat, he slipped and fell, breaking his collarbone. He initially said he fell while carrying groceries, which was not entirely untrue in hindsight, before clarifying the details.

Surgery effectively derailed his strong NL Rookie of the Year candidacy.

The Headline: Kicker Tears ACL Celebrating First-Quarter Field Goal

The Details: With roughly seven minutes remaining in the first quarter of a scoreless game between the Arizona Cardinals and New York Giants, rookie Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica kicked a 42-yard field goal.

Over-the-top celebrations on made kicks, whether they came in the clutch or while the smoke was still settling from pregame introductions, were part of the Bill Gramatica experience. On this occasion, he landed awkwardly after a celebratory jump and tore his ACL and medial meniscus in his right knee.

"You said I got hurt jumping. My jump was excellent. It was my landing I needed to work on," Gramatica told reporters in 2010, finding some levity in the years since the injury.

13. Antonio Brown (NFL) and Rickey Henderson (MLB)

The Headline: Frostbite 2, Superstar Athletes 0

The Details: A few weeks after joining the Blue Jays at the 1993 trade deadline, Rickey Henderson fouled a ball off the top of his foot in a game against the Twins on Aug. 12.

He went to the trainer's room the next day to treat his sore foot, but he accidentally left it on a synthetic ice pack too long, causing what amounted to freezer burn or frostbite . He played that night, but the burn eventually became so sore that he missed the next three games.

Former NFL star Antonio Brown was five years old when that happened. He apparently missed that story in the morning paper.

In July 2019, Brown suffered "extreme frostbite" on both feet after entering a cryotherapy chamber barefoot. The injuries kept him out for much of a tumultuous preseason, during which he was released before he made his Raiders debut.

The Headline: Wide Receiver Crashes Car Trying to Save Pizzas

The Details: A single-car accident involving an athlete is often the setup to a depressing fall from grace, but in the case of Lions wide receiver Nate Burleson, it was one of the most relatable weird injuries of all time.

Driving home from watching Monday Night Football at around 2:25 a.m. on Sept. 24, 2013, Burleson had two pizzas riding shotgun with him, stacked on top of one another. When the top pizza started to slide, he tried to adjust it before it fell, and he crashed into a median wall .

Burleson suffered a fractured forearm and ended up missing seven games. No alcohol, no drugs, not even a citation from the police officer who arrived on the scene. Just a man trying to save a pizza from falling and paying a steep price.

11. Lionel Simmons (NBA) and Joel Zumaya (MLB)

The Headline: Athletes and Tendinitis and Video Games, Oh My!

The Details: After a prolific collegiate career in which he scored 3,217 points over four seasons at La Salle, Lionel Simmons was selected seventh overall in the 1990 NBA draft by the Kings.

He averaged 18.0 points and 8.8 rebounds during his rookie season, though the lasting takeaway from that campaign is that he missed two games after developing tendinitis in his wrist and forearm from excessive use of his Nintendo Game Boy.

Video games grew and evolved in the years that followed, but became no less addictive. Just ask flame-throwing Tigers reliever Joel Zumaya.

With a 1.94 ERA in 83.1 innings over 62 appearances, Zumaya was a key cog in Detroit's bullpen as a rookie in 2006. The team reached the ALCS, and after pitching in Game 1, he missed the next three games with wrist and forearm inflammation.

Sound familiar? The culprit this time: Guitar Hero ... allegedly.

However, in a 2016 interview with the Detroit News , Zumaya called the Guitar Hero story "bogus" and hinted at it disguising a different root cause of the injury, but he refused to disclose what actually happened.

The Headline: MLB Outfielder Burns Face in Tanning Bed...Or Does He?

The Details: If there's one thing baseball fans remember about Marty Cordova's brief big league career, it's his stellar 1995 season that won him AL Rookie of the Year honors for the Twins.

If there are two things they remember, it's that and the story of him burning his face in a tanning bed.

Why did an athlete who spends his summers basking in the sun-drenched outfield of MLB stadiums feel the need to catch a few more rays on his off day? As it turns out, it was a cover.

In 2022, he finally set the record straight, clarifying that he actually got burned from laser surgery to remove ingrown facial hairs. That meant he had to avoid playing day games while the burns healed.

The Headline: NASCAR Legend Injured in Low-Speed Crash

The Details: The high-speed nature of NASCAR means any crash can be potentially serious or even life-threatening.

The low speed of golf carts means crashes are almost always avoidable and the result of shenanigans.

Shortly after winning his first NASCAR Cup Series championship in 2006, Jimmie Johnson was playing in a celebrity golf tournament when a cart crash left him with a broken wrist.

"I was in a golf cart and the driver took a sharp turn," Johnson told reporters . "I wasn't holding on tight enough, landed awkwardly on the ground and heard a little pop."

As it turns out, he wasn't holding on tight enough because he was on top of the golf cart , attempting to surf his way to the next hole. When he went to get down, his golf cleats slipped on the cart's plastic roof, and he fell directly onto his wrist.

The Headline: Arachnophobia Sends MLB Outfielder Through Glass Table

The Details: Outfielder Glenallen Hill was in his first full season in the majors, trying to carve out a regular role with the Blue Jays during the 1990 season when a bizarre incident sent him to the injured list.

Sleepwalking amid a nightmare about spiders, he ran into another room of his house and crashed through a glass coffee table . He suffered serious cuts and bruises that sidelined him for 14 games.

Decades later, broadcasters and sports fans alike still regularly mention it as one of the strangest sports injuries of all time.

While the incident remains Hill's enduring legacy for many, a monstrous rooftop home run at Wrigley Field and an absurd 1.112 OPS with 16 home runs in 40 games for the Yankees as a trade-deadline pickup in 2000 paint a more well-rounded picture of his 13-year career.

The Headline: Star Pass-Rusher Loses Fingers in Fireworks Accident

The Details: Honestly, it's surprising there have not been more fireworks-related accidents among athletes. An estimated 13,000 Americans were injured by fireworks in 2025 alone, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission .

There have certainly been others, but Jason Pierre-Paul stands alone atop the podium of the highest-profile fireworks injury in sports history.

A two-time Pro Bowler coming off a 12.5-sack season the previous year, JPP was one of the league's top pass-rushers when a Fourth of July fireworks mishap ended up costing him "2½" fingers and a two-week stint in the hospital to undergo multiple surgeries.

Impressively, he returned to the Giants later that season and went on to play 105 more games in the NFL. He even earned another Pro Bowl nod in 2020 when he tallied 9.5 sacks, four forced fumbles and two interceptions.

The Headline: MLB Knuckleballer ≠ Professional Strongman

The Details: Trying to inspire a team coming off a 90-loss season, the Brewers brass brought in a motivational group of strongmen known as "Radical Reality" during spring training in 1994.

As part of their presentation, they ripped phone books in half with their bare hands, and pitcher Steve Sparks was indeed inspired .

He tried the feat of strength himself to an audience of chanting teammates, even cheating a bit to make the tear easier, but the resistance of the tearing motion caused him to dislocate his left (non-throwing) shoulder. The team immediately optioned him to minor league camp.

Sparks' potential 1994 debut was delayed until 1995, though he went on to have a nine-year career in the big leagues.

The Headline: Team Doctor Accidentally Punctures QB's Lung

The Details: Tyrod Taylor entered the 2020 NFL season with a tenuous hold on the Chargers' starting quarterback job by design. His role was to bridge the gap from longtime starter Philip Rivers to first-round pick Justin Herbert.

He led the team to a Week 1 victory over the Bengals, but he suffered two cracked ribs during the first drive of the game. Prior to the team's Week 2 game, the team doctor administered a pain-killing injection to his ribs, but there were " complications ," and Herbert was thrust into action.

The complications? The doctor accidentally punctured his lung while administering the injection. He ended up hospitalized.

Herbert threw for 311 yards against the Chiefs, while Taylor ended up taking just one more snap for the rest of the season. Luckily, the 37-year-old is still going strong. He's currently serving as backup to Jordan Love in Green Bay.

The Headline: Punter Cuts Leg on Coach's Locker Room Axe

The Details: An axe and an NFL locker room brimming with testosterone. What could go wrong?

In his first year as head coach of the Jacksonville Jaguars, Jack Del Rio brought an axe and an oak tree stump into the locker room with a simple motto for his players: Keep chopping wood.

The on-the-nose metaphor about grinding and enduring may have landed, but so too did the fact that there was a sharp object that the coach had openly invited his players to swing.

"We understood the meaning behind it," safety Donovin Darius told reporters . "That's why we welcomed it in there. NFL players are big kids anyway, and you bring a big toy in the locker room, we're going to play around with it."

Punter Chris Hanson took his turn swinging the axe one day and ended up burying it in his right leg . He was rushed to a local hospital for emergency surgery and stitches.

Hanson's season was over after five games. He returned the following season and played six more years in the NFL.

The Headline: Norwegian Soccer Player Injured Escaping Moose

The Details: Bymarka is a large nature reserve in Norway known for cross-country skiing, hiking and its scenic beauty.

While getting ready for World Cup qualifying in 1980 as a member of Norway's national team, defender Svein Grøndalen went for a morning jog through Bymarka. That scenery got a little too close for comfort.

He accidentally came upon on a moose, startling it and causing it to charge him. He sprinted away and dove down a hill, suffering a severe laceration to his left leg.

The resulting injuries required stitches, forcing him to withdraw from the national team as a result.

The Headline: Golfer Forgets Gravity Exists, Is Quickly Reminded

The Details: With 16 PGA Tour wins and 29 total professional victories, Bobby Cruickshank was an accomplished golfer who enjoyed a solid prime during the 1920s and 1930s.

He never won a major championship, but came close multiple times, including at the 1934 U.S. Open when he had the lead with seven holes to go.

On the 11th hole, it appears his ball was headed for a water hazard, but it perfectly nailed a rock in the pond and bounced onto the green. Surely a stroke of good luck worth celebrating!

Cruickshank threw his club up into the air, only for it to come right back down and hit him on the head, opening up a wound that required stitches . Play was delayed, as he ultimately settled for a third-place finish.

The Headline: NFL Lineman Temporarily Blinded By Referee's Flag

The Details: Many of the stories in these rankings have a predictable outcome that could be seen from miles away, or a comical turn after initially scary circumstances.

This one is just the true definition of wrong place, wrong time.

In his first season with the Cleveland Browns after signing a six-year, $27 million deal that made him one of the highest-paid linemen in football, Orlando Brown suffered what stands as the most bizarre injury in sports history.

With the 1999 season winding to a close on Dec. 19, referee Jeff Triplette threw a flag into the Cleveland backfield for a run-of-the-mill false start penalty. The flag, weighted with metal ball bearings, sailed through Brown's facemask and hit him directly in the right eye .

After leaving the field immediately following the injury, an enraged Brown, who feared he had been blinded, returned and shoved Triplette to the ground, earning an indefinite suspension .

The suspension was lifted when the severity of the injury was revealed, but Brown missed the next three seasons recovering. He filed a $200 million lawsuit against the NFL and came away with a multi-million-dollar settlement .

For the record, NFL flags are now filled with a small bag of sand. They made that change immediately after the incident.

articles.title: BS Meter on the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: NHL training camps open next week, and not a moment too soon for fans after a quiet August with little real hockey news, especially on the trade front.
articles.body:
NHL training camps open next week, and not a moment too soon for fans after a quiet August with little real hockey news, especially on the trade front.

Only three trades occurred in August , none involving established NHL players. The drought ended on Sept. 1, when the Nashville Predators shipped winger Luke Evangelista to the New Jersey Devils for two draft picks.

That move could awaken a slumbering trade market as NHL general managers evaluate their rosters before the puck officially drops on the 2026-27 regular season on Sept. 29.

Most of the recent trade speculation involved notable stars like Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebucyk, Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, and Minnesota Wild defenseman Quinn Hughes. They were among the players featured in our NHL Trade Targets Big Board for September 2026 .

Could one of those stars be moved this month? Follow along as we deploy our trusty BS Meter to separate fact from fiction.

Will the Boston Bruins Trade Mason Lohrei?

Trade rumors dogged Mason Lohrei through most of last season and into the early weeks of the offseason. That conjecture landed the 25-year-old Boston Bruins defenseman at No. 7 on our July NHL Trade Block Big Board .

The speculation died away as the summer progressed. On Aug. 22, Lohrei told The Boston Globe 's Jim McBride that he was looking forward to the challenge of earning a full-time spot on the Bruins' blue line after being a healthy scratch for several regular-season and playoff games in 2025-26.

RG Media's James Murphy reported on Sept. 7 that multiple league sources claimed Lohrei was again drawing interest in the trade market. He said Lohrei was in play last season when the Bruins attempted to acquire Rasmus Andersson from the Calgary Flames before he was traded to the Vegas Golden Knights.

Lohrei is in the final season of a two-year contract with an average annual value of $3.2 million. He's slated to become a restricted free agent next summer with arbitration rights.

The Bruins may not be shopping Lohrei, but they could be open to trade offers. They also have a crowded blue line this season, which could make him a trade chip to address other roster issues, such as depth at center.

Are the St. Louis Blues Interested in Alexander Nikishin?

Trade rumors have swirled around Alexander Nikishin since June following reports that the Carolina Hurricanes were considering whether to re-sign or peddle him. The speculation reached a point where a trade seemed certain, earning the 24-year-old defenseman the No. 4 spot on our August Trade Targets Big Board .

Nikishin is a restricted free agent after completing his entry-level contract and is ineligible to sign an offer sheet because he lacks the minimum number of NHL games. He had a promising debut last season with 11 goals and 33 points, but his role and playing time were reduced during the Hurricanes' Stanley Cup run.

The conjecture died down during a quiet August in the NHL trade market. However, persistent rumblings have linked Nikishin to the St. Louis Blues since July. Jeremy Rutherford of The Athletic first reported that the Blues were believed to be interested in the young blueliner.

On Sept. 1, Rutherford boldly predicted that the Blues would acquire and sign Nikishin. He claimed the 6'3", 218-pound left-shot blueliner was the type of defenseman that general manager Alexander Steen was looking for.

The Hurricanes could re-sign Nikishin or perhaps peddle him to another club. Nevertheless, the rumors linking him to the Blues haven't gone away. It wouldn't be surprising if he ends up in St. Louis on a bridge contract.

Since his trade request was reported in early June, Dylan Larkin has been a fixture in the offseason rumor mill. The 30-year-old Detroit Red Wings center sits at No. 2 on our NHL Trade Targets Big Board for September 2026 . His request is currently in limbo as the Red Wings search for a new general manager.

Larkin is signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.7 million. He has a full no-movement clause, but will waive it for the Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers, and Vegas Golden Knights. The Dallas Stars are also rumored as a possible landing spot.

However, Larkin's preferred destinations lack the salary cap space and tradeable assets to acquire him. Some observers suggest he must widen his list if he hopes to be traded before the regular season begins, assuming the Red Wings have hired a new GM by then.

On Aug. 28, NHL Network's Mike Johnson suggested the Montréal Canadiens as a trade destination if Larkin wants to play for a Stanley Cup contender. He noted that the Canadiens are loaded with young talent to be a contender for several years. They can draw on some of it to make a tempting offer to the Red Wings.

Larkin's list of landing spots is all American-based teams. He's unlikely to join the Canadiens or any other Canadian franchises. If he has to widen his trade list, it probably won't include clubs north of the border.

Will the Minnesota Wild Trade Quinn Hughes If They Can't Re-Sign Him?

The uncertainty over Quinn Hughes' future with the Minnesota Wild earned him the No. 13 spot on our September NHL Trade Targets Big Board . As training camp approaches without a contract extension for the 26-year-old superstar defenseman, trade speculation continues to brew about his future.

On Aug. 31, Wild general manager Bill Guerin acknowledged that defenseman Cale Makar's record-setting contract with the Colorado Avalanche set a bar for Hughes. However, he also said Hughes was a different personality who wanted different things out of life. "Who knows what he's gonna want in the end," Guerin said.

NHL insider Frank Seravalli told Sportsnet that he felt the Wild should sign Hughes soon or move on from him. He suggested the New Jersey Devils as a potential trade or free-agent destination, citing that Hughes' brothers, Jack and Luke, play for the Devils.

The Athletic's Michael Russo reported that Guerin remained confident he can get Hughes re-signed. However, while the blueliner still believes in the Wild and praised Guerin and the team, he won't be rushed into signing an extension, saying he wants to make the right decision for everyone involved.

The longer Hughes goes without an extension, the more questions will be raised about whether he really wants to stay in Minnesota. If his reluctance stretches into the New Year, Guerin could feel the pressure to move him before the March 1 trade deadline.

Could the Winnipeg Jets Have Difficulty Trading Connor Hellebuyck?

Perched atop our September NHL Trade Targets Big Board , Connor Hellebucyk's days with the Winnipeg Jets appear to be numbered. He revealed last month that he requested a trade this spring and still believes it would be best for him and his family to move to another NHL city.

Hellebuyck, 33, should attract plenty of interest in the trade market. An elite goaltender, he's the league's only active three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also won the Hart Memorial Trophy in 2024-25 and backstopped Team USA to gold in the 2026 Winter Olympics.

While Hellebuyck has a full no-movement clause , Chris Johnston of The Athletic reported on Aug. 27 that he's willing to waive it for "a variety of teams". His colleague, Pierre LeBrun, reported that the Carolina Hurricanes, Buffalo Sabres, and Utah Mammoth are among the possibilities.

However, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman told NHL Network last Friday that the trade options open to the Jets earlier this summer are no longer available . He also noted that some players who may have been available before July 1 may no longer be because their no-trade clauses had changed.

Friedman believed the Florida Panthers were interested in Hellebuyck but used most of their trade capital to acquire Brady Tkachuk. The Jets discussed a deal with the Buffalo Sabres, but Friedman said a disagreement about swapping 2026 first-round picks scuttled that plan.

Salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Philadelphia 76ers shooting guard preview: VJ Edgecombe, bench unit
articles.summary: It's time to look at the shooting guards for the Philadelphia 76ers led by VJ Edgecombe and the depth in the bench unit.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 season is quickly approaching for the Philadelphia 76ers as they have their eyes on ending a long title drought after the big additions made in the offseason. The Sixers will field one of the more talented rosters in the league and will look to get to the mountaintop in 2027.

It's now time to look ahead to the new season and time to break down each position for the Sixers in an effort to preview what the season might look like. Sixers Wire will look at the shooting guards now and take a look at what the Sixers bring to the table at the position:

Edgecombe had one of the more impressive rookie seasons anybody will see for a player so young and surrounded by so many veterans. When a player is selected as high as Edgecombe was, at No. 3, that player is normally the foundational piece for a team to build around. In his situation, he joined a Sixers team with established stars and veterans as he looked to find a niche, and he was able to make a huge splash throughout the season and into the playoffs.

Edgecombe vowed when the season ended to work on his jumper. He did shoot a respectable 35.4% from deep in the regular season, but that number dropped to 29.2% in the playoffs. He has shot the ball well while playing for the Bahamas in the FIBA World Qualifiers and that is an encouraging sign for Philadelphia because if he becomes a knockdown shooter, then his game gets elevated to another level. He has been in the gym all summer and will look to bring that type of production to the Sixers in his second season.

The Sixers were able to snag 2-time champ Kentavious Caldwell-Pope in free agency after a year with the Memphis Grizzlies . The 13-year veteran is a reliable player who will likely shoot the ball better in Philadelphia than he did in Memphis (31.6% from deep). His shooting numbers have dropped a bit, but one has to believe him being in a winning situation like the Sixers will allow him to find his groove again.

Anfernee Simons will also see some time here as he brings his microwave scoring ability to the City of Brotherly Love. He can knock down shots from all over the court and has the ability to really light up a scoreboard. He's averaged over 20 points twice in his career. Two-way player Caleb Love provides depth here as well after averaging 10.4 points as a rookie in Portland .

articles.title: Broncos' 2nd-year pass rusher trending up: 'Nobody can block him'
articles.summary: "Whenever he sets his mind to it, nobody can block him," Broncos OLB Nik Bonitto said of Que Robinson.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos might have a breakout candidate at outside linebacker this fall.

Que Robinson (6-4, 243 pounds), who was picked by the Broncos in the fourth round of last year's NFL draft out of Alabama and impressed in his limited playing time as a rookie, is set to get more snaps in Year 2.

"Que is obviously a very talented guy," Broncos pass rusher Nik Bonitto said in August. "He's showing out every day in practice. He has all the tools, and whenever he sets his mind to it, nobody can block him. He's been playing really well right now, and I'm excited especially to see these next couple of games what he does out there. I know he's going to put on a show for sure."

With Jonathon Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list and ineligible to play, Bonitto and Jonah Elliss will serve as the team's starters going into the 2026 season. Robinson and Dondrea Tillman will rotate in behind them, and there will be plenty of snaps to go around between the four pass rushers.

"The guy I've been super impressed with, and I've told him, is Que Robinson," Denver tight end Evan Engram said last week when asked which defensive player made the biggest improvement this offseason. "He's been a force all camp. There have been a couple of times I've been in pass protection, and he's lined up across and I've had to bring it and lock in. He's definitely growing as a player, and he has a bright future ahead of him for sure."

Elliss is poised to start in the place of Cooper, but Robinson will be another key player to watch early in the season. The Broncos are set to open the campaign on Monday Night Football against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 14 .

articles.title: Clippers Insider Makes It Clear Who’s To Blame For Bradley Beal Taking Chris Paul’s Number
articles.summary: Law Murray says Bradley Beal shouldn’t be blamed for wearing number 3 because the Clippers made it available.
articles.body:
Bradley Beal has already gotten plenty of criticism and mockery for taking Chris Paul's number 3 jersey with the Los Angeles Clippers , but The Athletic's Law Murray thinks the anger is being directed at the wrong person.

Appearing on The Zach Lowe Show , Murray defended Beal and instead placed the responsibility on the Clippers organization for allowing Paul's iconic number to immediately come back into circulation.

"Even right now, they are not showing that they are interested in even addressing their fans in any way possible. You know, everything has been defensive about what has come out."

"And I mean, I don't even put this on Brad because Brad gave up his number last year. He was here before Chris, and they have a great relationship. And, you know, Brad wore zero so Chris could have his number. This isn't about Brad."

"This is about who makes these decisions to say, 'We're keeping this number out of circulation,' which they did when Chris wasn't here for seven years. And now, the first offseason Chris is done playing, they give this number."

"So Brad's taking the heat, but let's apply the heat where it absolutely should be. And that's on a Clippers team that has been increasingly tone-deaf over the last couple of years."

Context is very important. Bradley Beal had worn number 3 throughout his NBA career with the Washington Wizards and the Phoenix Suns . Yet when Paul returned to the Clippers last season, he switched to zero so Paul could continue wearing his iconic number 3 jersey.

Now that Paul has retired, Beal is returning to number 3, which has prompted criticism from fans who think the Clippers should have preserved that number for arguably their greatest player in franchise history.

But Murray argues that the decision should entirely belong to the organization, and that seems to be the strangest part of this entire situation. Paul left the Clippers in 2017, but after that, they did not hand number 3 to another player during his long absence. Yet after returning for his farewell season and retiring, that jersey was immediately made available to Beal.

Paul's relationship with the franchise has also made the optics really worse. His final Clippers stint ended after only 16 games, and Paul later described the way he was treated as one of the most disrespectful experiences of his career.

Beal has already pushed back on suggestions that him wearing number 3 disrespects Chris Paul . Even Murray appears to agree with Beal's position, and his issue is now with how the Clippers have handled the situation.

The Clippers are facing a lot of scrutiny following their salary cap circumvention scandal involving Kawhi Leonard , making another PR controversy very poorly timed.

The Clippers also remain the only NBA franchise without an official player jersey retired. Outside of Bill Russell's league-wide number 6 jersey, which was retired after the legend passed away, Paul would seemingly be the obvious candidate to become their first.

Whatever eventually happens, Murray's message is straightforward: Beal did not disrespect Paul by reclaiming his longtime number. The Clippers were the ones with the authority to keep number 3 out of circulation, and instead they chose not to.

articles.title: Expert predictions, picks for Florida football vs Campbell in Week 2
articles.summary: Here are the Gators Wire staff's predictions and picks for college football's Week 2 matchup between the Florida Gators and Campbell Fighting Camels.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the college football season has the Florida Gators lined up to face the Campbell Camels inside Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday. It will be the first time that the Orange and Blue have faced the FCS school, and the matchup comes before the SEC schedule begins next week on the road against Auburn.

Florida has amassed a 25-1 record across 26 contests against FCS opponents since 1981, with the lone loss over that span coming against Georgia Southern in 2013. The Gators have outscored their FCS opponents by an average margin of 39.3 points and have eclipsed 450 total yards in five straight while rushing for over 150 yards in nine in a row.

While Florida looked good in the 2026 season opener, there is still room for improvement. Sumrall and Co. will be looking to smooth the edges — particularly on defense — before embarking on their conference journey. What better way to hone their weapons than against an FCS opponent?

With all of that in mind, the Gators Wire staff convened to offer their expert opinion on the upcoming matchup. Here is what we had to offer.

'It is hard to see the Gators falling short against Campbell'

After the offensive domination witnessed in Week 1 against FAU, it is hard to see the Gators falling short against Campbell in Week 2. Sure, Florida has some wrinkles to work out in its defense and there is still some room for improvement to be made on the other side of the ball, but this team seems to be trending in the right direction early on.

The key to this matchup is that Sumrall and Co. use their FCS opponent to prepare for the upcoming SEC gauntlet. Things get tough really quickly, starting with a road matchup with Auburn in Week 3, so now is the time to tie up any loose ends that the Gators might have. — Adam Dubbin

'Expect the defense to make their statement this game'

The Florida offense was arguably one of the best that was on display from an SEC team this past weekend, and the sentiment should still hold, if not explode even more, against Campbell. Points should come seamlessly, and I expect to see Tramell Jones Jr. earlier in this game than in the previous outing.

Florida's main concern in the win over FAU was its defense, and I expect the Gators to be cleaner around the edges as they prepare for SEC play the following week. Expect the defense to make their statement this game. — Michael Trim Jr .

'Florida controls the game from start to finish'

Go! Go! Go! Florida's offense had one speed in the opening week and there's little reason to believe Campbell has the personnel to slow down Jadan Baugh, Vernell Brown III and the rest of the Gators' wealth of weapons. I expect Buster Faulkner to continue opening up the offense while getting several young players meaningful opportunities before SEC play begins.

My biggest focus rests on Florida's defensive front. Perhaps a game against inferior competition will be just what the unit needs to spring forward as big-time football ramps up Week 3 and beyond. It's fair to say the Gators' front struggled against FAU — Gerald Chatman's group was rendered ineffective for much of the game and Caden Veltkamp looked far too comfortable in the pocket against an SEC rush. The run defense wasn't stellar either, with the Owls finding success on the ground in spurts. Saturday will be a chance for the group to respond and show improvement.

Dallas Wilson should benefit from Eric Singleton's absence and I'd love to see Pryor and Clark gain confidence in the second half after Baugh continues making his Heisman case. Florida controls the game from start to finish, minus a few hiccups that surfaced against FAU. Sumrall keeps his foot on the gas to drive home an outspoken message for this team heading into Auburn. — Michael Long

'There's little reason to expect anything other than a blowout'

There's little reason to expect anything other than a blowout this week against Campbell. The offense looks good under Buster Faulkner, and now the players have actual game reps. Much to my surprise, Aaron Philo handled the deep ball well, and not having Eric Singleton for most of the game proved inconsequential. Another three-tuddy day for Jadan Baugh would be nice, but this is the game I'd get the backups in a bit earlier.

Defensively, things need to be tighter, and I expect they will be. Playing closer on third down and giving max effort throughout the game is the only option if this group is going to improve.

articles.title: 3 defensive keys for Texas A&M against Arizona State in Week 2
articles.summary: Texas A&M’s defense must contain Cutter Boley and prevent Arizona State’s explosive playmakers from taking over Saturday’s matchup.
articles.body:
The Texas A&M defense dominated its Week 1 opponent, holding the Missouri State Bears to 67 yards, four first downs and 1.7 yards per play. Arizona State will face a significant step up in competition after showing a balanced attack and posting 681 yards in its 70-7 win over Morgan State.

Sun Devils quarterback Cutter Boley had a monster debut , completing 21 of 27 passes for 387 yards and six touchdowns. Three ASU receivers surpassed 100 receiving yards and scored at least one touchdown. The Sun Devils also ran for 249 yards, presenting enough balance to challenge the Aggie defense at every level.

As head coach Mike Elko indicated, there are levels to college football, and Missouri State was not equipped to truly test a Texas A&M defense that Elko believes is his deepest since arriving in Aggieland. ASU has enough talent to make this game interesting despite entering as the underdog. If the Aggies want to keep the game under control, they will need to key in on the following areas.

Key 1: Prevent explosive plays and tackle in space

ASU was a big-play machine in Week 1, recording a ridiculous 10 plays of at least 25 yards and 365 yards after the catch. Reed Harris, Grayson Rigdon and Omarion Miller each surpassed 100 receiving yards. Rigdon was the most efficient, turning two catches into 110 yards and two touchdowns.

The Sun Devils pride themselves on blocking downfield and helping spring explosive plays. The Aggie secondary must keep ASU's receivers in front of it, close quickly and finish tackles. If it does not, the Sun Devils can turn a short pass into a 50-yard gain in a hurry.

Boley finished his ASU debut with 387 yards, six touchdowns and a 77.8% completion rate. However, you have to consider the level of competition. During his final season at Kentucky, Boley showed plenty of talent but went 4-6 as the starter while throwing 15 touchdowns and 12 interceptions and taking 26 sacks.

Arizona State's offensive line entered this season with only 33 combined career starts. If the Aggies can take advantage of that inexperience, they should be able to generate consistent pressure, disrupt Boley's timing and force him into mistakes.

This might be the biggest key of the three because ASU's running back rotation combined for 249 yards and averaged 7.1 yards per carry. The Sun Devils use a committee approach, which makes them more difficult to prepare for than an offense built around one featured back.

Winning on first down will be paramount for the Aggies. Slowing the running game can create predictable passing situations and give Texas A&M better opportunities to pressure Boley.

This is the type of early-season test Texas A&M needs before entering conference play. If the Aggies tackle well, pressure Boley and keep ASU behind schedule, they should be able to prevent the explosive plays that powered the Sun Devils' Week 1 performance.

articles.title: Broncos 2026 season preview: Raining vengeance upon the football gods
articles.summary: Bo Nix's ankle injury turned 2025 into a "what if?". Now revenge is within Denver's grasp.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos understood completely. The worst pain comes from hope. Like the hope of seeing a young franchise quarterback pilot his team to a home date in the AFC Championship Game, only to cede his place to a backup due to injury.

That's what happened last January. Bo Nix suffered a broken ankle late in Denver's 33-30 Divisional Round win over the Buffalo Bills . Jarrett Stidham replaced him to face his former team on a snowy afternoon in Colorado. The Broncos held the New England Patriots to only 10 points and lost anyway.

Denver could have held tight and run it back for 2026. Instead, the Broncos got proactive. They traded for a 27-year-old wide receiver with three 1,000-yard seasons to his name. Another talented wideout who can win one-on-one should help Nix from hitting a wall and reduce the team's reliance on play-action fakes and roll-outs, establishing him as a more stable pocket presence and giving head coach Sean Payton the Drew Brees surrogate to get him back to the Super Bowl.

Denver's WR2-by-committee behind Courtland Sutton was occasionally electric but often inconsistent. Now Troy Franklin , Pat Bryant and Marvin Mims will fight to be Bo Nix's third target in an offense that continues to add ways to beat you.

Waddle's average target distance rose as he emerged as the Dolphins ' top receiver last fall, filling some of the role Tyreek Hill left behind (albeit with mixed results. Bringing some extra deep ball credibility for a quarterback who has polished his bomb-lobbing skills after being criticized for a low-impact passing game at Oregon. It should also set the stage for a player like Franklin, Bryant or Mims to shine in the space created, even if snaps in the Broncos offense suddenly became harder to find.

Denver was arguably one injury away from a Super Bowl appearance and paying a quarterback on a rookie contract, so it largely kept the band together for 2026. Swapping out Joe Lombardi for Davis Webb at offensive coordinator could create issues, but Sean Payton's history suggests a smooth transition.

Instead, let's look at the underappreciated Franklin-Myers. The defensive lineman has been a consistent pressure generator from his end spot, and while his pressure rate dipped to a career-low 11 percent last season — still good! — his 7.5 sacks were third-most on the team. Can recent third round picks Tyler Onyedim and Sai'vion Jones fill the void he leaves?

JK Dobbins remains electric. He also remains injury prone. RJ Harvey was one of the league's least efficient runners, racking up -89 rushing yards over expected (RYOE) in just 146 carries (though he was an asset in the passing game).

That leaves room for the fourth round rookie to shine. Coleman is a bowling ball of a runner with a hard-charging first step and the power to blast through rapidly closing holes to keep his offense on schedule. He may not be a sensation right away, but he'll be ready when opportunity knocks.

QB rank (expected points added per dropback, via RBSDM.com ): 18

Yes, but only a little. There's not much room to improve when you were one injury away from a potential Super Bowl invitation.

articles.title: Commanders vs. Eagles: 3 reasons for optimism in Week 1
articles.summary: There are three reasons for optimism for the Washington Commanders when they face the Philadelphia Eagles this Sunday in Week 1 action.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is finally upon us, and the Washington Commanders open the season on the road when they face the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Stadium in Philadelphia , Pennsylvania, at 4:25 p.m. EDT this Sunday.

The Commanders have fielded questions all offseason about almost everything they've done and every change they've made. Adam Peters set out to make the defense younger and faster, and while the team is still one of the older teams in the league, it's younger than it was last season. The offense saw fewer changes, but enough of them to make an impact on the field, especially signing Stefon Diggs during training camp.

Still, opening the season on the road against a division rival is tough. They have a lot to prove this season, and the Eagles are no small obstacle to overcome. Playing in a hostile environment makes things harder, but the Commanders are ready to prove the league wrong. They have a chip on their shoulder, and they're using every disrespectful ranking and comment as fuel to win. That said, let's take a look at three reasons for optimism for the Commanders in Week 1.

It's no secret this team plays better when Daniels is healthy, and when they faced the Eagles in 2025, Daniels didn't play in either game. This year, Daniels has a new offensive coordinator in David Blough and has reportedly looked comfortable operating the new under-center, motion-heavy offense.

On top of that, Daniels has new weapons in Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo , rookie wide receiver Antonio Willilams, and veteran running back Rachaad White , who offers a legitimate option out of the backfield. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is first on the depth chart at running back, but they each play a different role when on the field. Let's not forget Daniels' ability to use his own legs, too. Even though the goal is to keep him in the pocket, the Eagles have to consider that he might take off with the ball at any moment.

If Blough uses motion, play action, moves players around, and uses his tight ends, the Commanders can stress out the Eagles' defense horizontally. Forcing Philly to defend the entire field instead of letting Jalen Carter and the defensive line dictate the game will be key.

This is something no one is really talking about. The Eagles are on their fifth offensive coordinator in Nick Sirianni's sixth season as head coach, and they traded A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots during the offseason. That makes DeVonta Smith the No. 1 wide receiver, with Dontayvion Wicks (first year with Philly) and rookie Makai Lemon as additional starting receivers. The offense has a different dynamic without Brown.

Saquon Barkley will be a problem for opposing defenses for as long as he's in the NFL; that goes without saying. But Daronte Jones is expected to bring a more aggressive, pressure-oriented approach that will impact how the Eagles call the game. This will be the new Eagles offense versus the new Commanders defense.

If Washington can force Philadelphia into obvious passing situations, it can unleash its pass rush and make life uncomfortable for Jalen Hurts .

As mentioned above, Adam Peters revamped the Commanders' defense during the offseason. There are eight new potential starters, including Nick Cross , Odafe Oweh , K'Lavon Chaisson, Leo Chenal , and, possibly, Sonny Styles . Jones' defensive scheme will not only be focused on creating pressure, but Jones is also expected to use more creative coverage and pressure packages, making it difficult to discern what the defense is going to do.

The Commanders don't necessarily need to shut down the Eagles' offense, although that is the goal, but they need to create uncertainty. Force Philadelphia to question what they are doing, to wonder where the pressure is coming from, who is blitzing, who's dropping, and whether it's man or zone coverage. With the Eagles installing a new system, confusion can be enough to throw them off.

If Jones can make Hurts process rather than react, Washington has a chance to keep this game tight.

Juventus 's ongoing and seemingly midfield injury crisis could see Pape Sarr make his debut for the Old Lady sooner than Luciano Spalletti would have liked.

The Senegal international arrived from Spurs with a hamstring strain and has just returned to training. As reported by Corriere dello Sport , Spalletti is considering whether to take him with the squad for the trip to Sassuolo as a bench option, with an eye on handing him his debut against Nijmegen in the Europa League next week.

Manuel Locatello and Khéphren Thuram have recently underwent surgeries and are expected to remain out until at least the turn of the year. Locatelli has had surgery for a lateral meniscus tear in right knee, while Thuram underwent surgery to treat chondropathy of the patella , also in his right knee.

Weston McKennie , returning from a muscular issue, could be available for the Sassuolo game, while Douglas Luiz and Teun Koopmeiners are expected to start against the Neroverdi .

For the coming weeks, Spalletti will have to chop and change and look for several combinations in the middle of the park, hoping no new hiccups occur after what have been a cataclysmic injury-ridden weeks to kick off the new season.

OGC Nice are considering a move for Stade Rennais defender Alidu Seidu (26), according to a report from L'Équipe .

Rules in France would permit the recruitment of the Ghana international, despite the closure of the transfer window in France on 1st September. Clubs are allowed to recruit a 'joker', should certain conditions be met. One of those conditions is a severe injury within the current squad. Antoine Mendy suffered an ACL injury during last weekend's draw against Le Mans, which would allow Le Gym to dip into the market.

Seidu is currently on the fringes at Rennes and he has now been made a priority target by Nice. The Côte d'Azur club are currently waiting for their budget to be validated by their owners, INEOS, before making their move for the defender. A loan deal with a buy option could be struck between the two parties, as per L'Équipe. Seidu's deal runs until 2029.

articles.title: Oregon State prepping for another top-25 opponent in Texas Tech
articles.summary: Oregon State will take on No. 13 Texas Tech in Week 2 of the college football season Sept. 12 at Reser Stadium in Corvallis.
articles.body:
Oregon State's breakout wide receiver earned some conference accolades after his collegiate debut.

Jesse Legree, a freshman from Baltimore , posted 136 receiving yards and a touchdown in the Beavers' 33-20 loss to top 25-ranked Houston . Days later, Legree was named the Pac-12 freshman of the week.

Oregon State head coach JaMarcus Shephard has been raving about Legree since the spring.

"I don't understand why you guys wouldn't believe me when I'm saying the kid's going to be good. It makes zero sense to me why you would even second guess that," Shephard said.

Shephard's resume with freshmen wide receivers has been more than stellar throughout his career. Rondale Moore , a former Purdue standout currently on the Minnesota Vikings , earned all-American honors as a freshman with Shephard as his coach. David Bell , another Purdue alum and current NFL player, was Big 10 freshman of the year. Ryan Williams, an Alabama eye-popping receiver, received all-conference and freshman all-American honors with Shephard at the helm.

So for Shephard, he's had his eye on Legree as one of the next great freshman receivers and was far from surprised about his output against Houston .

"We knew that he's just got a mentality about himself, being from the DMV … we just knew that throughout all of spring ball, camp, he just played like a veteran," Shephard said.

But now, Shephard anticipates future defenses to tailor to the potential of Legree's game. When No. 13 Texas Tech comes to Reser Stadium in Corvallis Sept. 12, the Oregon State offense will have to call on Legree and its plethora of receiving talent to connect with quarterback Braden Atkinson in order to compete.

Against Houston, Atkinson completed 29 of 48 passes to nine different receivers for 376 yards and a touchdown.

Oregon State's sideline-to-sideline, fast-paced, often-throwing offense found a groove in the second half of the game in Houston — and it seems like a sign of what's to come.

"We've got a lot of young men who can do a lot of different things for our offense," Shephard said. "Each one of them just needs to work on doing their job. We expect multiple guys to contribute … we don't want to allow an opponent to just focus on one person. We just can't allow that."

Shephard has full confidence in Atkinson's ability to spread the football. Shephard described some of Atkinson's traits in the first game as present, focused and calm.

"The leadership piece of our football team was shown by not just our coaches … but also our captains and especially our quarterback," Shephard said. "Our quarterback was a guy who I felt like controlled the game very well. He did a really good job of executing the plays exactly how we wanted it to be done and he did it with a lot of precision."

There's even an acronym floating around the Beavers ' offense for Atkinson; F.T.S.

"We weren't telling him he had to throw to a specific person. We just had him go through his reads like he's supposed to and deliver the ball to the individual who he's supposed to deliver it to based on what the reads are," Shephard said. "He needs to be the distribution center of the football, that's his job."

Oregon State's second game will be its second against a top-25 opponent. The Beavers left the first game with some notes — in the run game, on the lines, in the defensive backfield — but Shephard looks forward to finding answers.

Houston quarterback Connor Weigman went for 305 passing yards and a touchdown and helped a pair of receivers garner over 80 yards, including Amare Thomas, who went for 133 yards and a touchdown.

Houston also had two rushers gain over 75 yards apiece.

"As I told (our team) as we were getting off the plane, we're better than that," Shephard said. "We're a better football team than what we played on Saturday and I was very emphatic about that. I'm continuing to let them know we're a better football team than what we showed on Saturday."

In Texas Tech's season-opening 33-10 win over Abiline Christian, the Red Raiders were efficient in a various facets of the game.

Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond completed 26 of 33 passes for 298 yards and a touchdown. Ten different receivers caught a pass from Hammond and three of them gained over 50 yards total.

In the run game, two different Texas Tech rushers scored touchdowns and three had 10 or more carries. It's an offense that tried to find balance and will look to execute at an even higher level Saturday in Corvallis.

Texas Tech's defense, similarly, executed well with three sacks, an interception and just 10 points allowed. In an effort to not let the defense get into rhythm, Shephard said the Oregon State offense must start fast.

"It's really a pillar of our program," Shephard said. "When you talk about those three things: starting fast, the middle eight and finishing strong. We've got to be better in all three phases of that ... I think that they figured it out as the game was going along. I think they started out really slow, I felt like we weren't as fast early in the game, and we got faster as the game went on."

Last year, Texas Tech defeated Oregon State 45-14 in Lubbock, Texas. The Red Raiders were ranked then like they are now but for Oregon State, a new coaching staff and new roster takes on a familiar top-25 opponent exactly a year after the last contest.

How to watch Oregon State vs. Texas Tech

Oregon State vs. Texas Tech will air on CBS at 4:30 p.m. PT Sept. 12 from Reser Stadium in Corvallis.

Streaming options include Fubo , DirecTV, YouTube TV or Paramount+.

articles.title: Patriots injury analysis after season opener vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Analyzing the Patriots’ injury situation after their Week 1 loss.
articles.body:
Their season opener against the Seattle Seahawks did not go the way the New England Patriots would have hoped. Not only did they let a 10-0 lead slip out of their grasp behind a three-interception performance from their starting quarterback, they also lost one of their most important offensive skill position players to what projects as a multi-week injury.

Obviously, all eyes are on A.J. Brown and his sprained ankle coming out of the game. But as a look at our weekly injury analysis shows, he was not the only Patriot to get banged up during the 13-10 defeat on Wednesday night .

CB Carlton Davis III: Davis was shaken up midway through the first quarter while helping to blow up a run play. He remained down on one knee, but jogged off with members of New England's training staff shortly thereafter. Following a brief stay in the blue medical tent, he returned to the sidelines and eventually reentered. the contest on the next defensive series.

TE Hunter Henry : Henry took a hard hit on the first play from scrimmage in the second half, landing on his back after a 13-yard reception. He left the field under his own power and entered the medical tent for further evaluation, but returned to the game a short time later.

WR A.J. Brown: The big one. Brown remained on the ground after an incomplete third-down attempt, with medical personnel and even head coach Mike Vrabel checking in on him on the field. He limped off the field into the medical tent, and later gingerly walked back to the locker room albeit under his own power. Follow-up evaluation done on Thursday found out that he had suffered a high-ankle sprain .

C Jared Wilson : The Patriots' starting center had to be evaluated on the sideline after suffering an apparent cut on his right snapping hand during the first series of the second half, the same that saw Henry and Brown get shaken up. He ended up playing all 71 offensive snaps.

RT Morgan Moses : During his Monday press conference, head coach Mike Vrabel listed Moses among other players suffering injuries in the game. There was no obvious moment an injury might have occurred, however, and he did end up playing 100% of New England's offensive snaps.

Losing A.J. Brown just 31 snaps into his Patriots debut is an obvious blow to an offense that already had a hard time stringing consistent plays together versus the Seahawks with him on the field. Now, the unit will have to find a way to operate with Romeo Doubs , DeMario Douglas , Mack Hollins , Kyle Williams and Efton Chism as its primary wide receivers — a group that will be in the spotlight over the coming games.

Based on Wednesday and his role throughout the summer, Williams in particular should see an uptick in reps as the primary X-receiver. Hollins, who does have some good chemistry with Drake Maye , also will continue to be heavily involved.

For how long Brown will be out remains to be seen. According to reports, the expected recovery range for his type of sprain is somewhere between four and six weeks. This means that short-term injured reserve, which would sideline him for a minimum of four weeks, appears to be a realistic if ultimately disappointing possibility.

As for the other players listed above, they do not appear to have suffered any long-term issues.

"Morgan Moses was able to return. Hunter Henry was able to return. Carlton Davis III was able to return," said Mike Vrabel on Thursday. "Probably some bumps and bruises, but I do not think anything that would keep anybody out. A.J. Brown is one we will have to monitor."

Coming off their season opener, the Patriots will enjoy a 10-day break before their home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

articles.title: Urban Meyer gives his take on Michigan Football’s QB situation
articles.summary: One of college football’s most controversial figures, Urban Meyer, had some opinions on Michigan Football’s quarterback situation:
articles.body:
If you're a fan of anyone that isn't Ohio State or Florida , that's a mildly concerning sentence. Despite being one of the most decorated college football coaches of the 21st century, Meyer is arguably just as known for his colorful personal life, rap sheet of ethical violations and deeply unpleasant personality as he is for the trio of national championships he's won between his tenures with the Gators and Buckeyes.

This week on The Triple Option Podcast , Meyer broke down the Wolverines ' quarterback situation and the relationship between head coach Kyle Whittingham and quarterback Bryce Underwood . And he had some interesting things to say.

Meyer began by emphasizing the strength of Whittingham's relationship with Underwood, stating that Whittingham made it clear he "loves" Underwood and the issues aren't related to coachability. He then commented on how he thinks Underwood's struggles as a freshman owed themselves heavily to the Wolverines' lack of quarterback coach. But it was his take on the quarterback situation around Underwood that'll raise some eyebrows.

"Everything you're saying is dictated by something who's behind him — it's Tommy Carr," Meyer said. "Coach Whitt really loves his kid, says he's got an incredible future. But he's also underdeveloped as far as physically. So we're making decisions without knowing what's — your job as a head coach is to win the next game; whoever gives you the best opportunity, play that human being. And I think Kyle will do that."

Following Underwood's underwhelming but ultimately heroic effort against Western Michigan , the naysayers came out in force, calling for Underwood's benching. As the backup to Underwood, brother of Heisman-contending Notre Dame star C.J. Carr and grandson of Michigan great Lloyd Carr, Tommy certainly has caught some eyes. He was a lightly recruited player and widely regarded as undersized, which Meyer took note of, but camp whisperers have suggested there's potentially something there.

Meyer then continued by breaking down the offensive line and run game as criteria that point to the ugly performance more than Underwood himself, before segueing into a scenario where Tommy could potentially challenge Underwood for his job.

"So there's, I don't know," Meyer said. "If you lose the game, you're right, you probably push that button down and implode the whole thing and start over. And that means a new quarterback, maybe new other position players, but you just don't know what's around them. I would, again, say this. They have to compete with Oklahoma ."

I wouldn't really go as far as to read this as a suggestion that Underwood is in danger, though. I think Meyer's take that the Wolverines should "push the button down and implode" should they lose to the Sooners is a bizarre take. Regardless of how bad Michigan has looked so far, I don't think there's a world where it's smart to hit the reset button just two games into a new coaching era. But the quote itself isn't really singling out Underwood as someone who is at a special risk of losing his job, rather than saying the entirety of the system could change with a loss. Still a strange take, but not necessarily anti-Underwood.

Meyer then closed out by saying he thinks Whittingham will "put people on the field that (he thinks) can win the game," and that Carr "is a guy that they feel can be a quarterback and lead them to a championship at some point."

Overall, I don't think any of what Meyer said was particularly reflective of Underwood's job being in jeopardy. But there are some clues that point toward Whittingham not being hesitant on making a change if a change is what he believes would help Michigan win games. Meyer and Whittingham are incredibly close, dating back to their time at Utah coaching together in the early-2000s. Meyer is about as dialed in with Whittingham as anyone, so the likelihood of Meyer talking with Whittingham before recording the podcast and forming his opinion based off Whittingham's comments is fairly high.

However, there's also a significant amount of coach-speak relating to Whittingham and the downright nonsensical suggestion that a loss to Oklahoma should trigger the nuclear option. But Underwood would simply be caught in the blast radius of that situation rather than the reason in and of himself for a change. In fact, Meyer is genuinely fairly positive towards Underwood.

So yeah. There you have it. To sum it up, Urban freaking Meyer is surprisingly more forgiving to Underwood than some elements of this fanbase. I'm not sure what that says about us.

articles.title: Who's to Blame For WWE Star Cody Rhodes' Downfall?
articles.summary: WWE Sunday Night's Main Event ended with the latest example of why Cody Rhodes desperately needs a new direction.
articles.body:
WWE Sunday Night's Main Event ended with the latest example of why Cody Rhodes desperately needs a new direction.

It has been a rough year for the second-generation wrestler, who had the world at his feet two years ago. Honestly, it's hard to make sense of the drastic jump from his triumph at WrestleMania 40 to his fortunes at the same event over the last two years.

Although Rhodes struck out at Royal Rumble and Elimination Chamber, he regained the WWE title to set up a highly anticipated match with Randy Orton. Unfortunately, their storyline inexplicably focused on Pat McAfee instead of their storied history.

Their showdown on The Grandest Stage of Them All was underwhelming, and Rhodes left the ring with a gruesome orbital injury. The 41-year-old didn't fare much better at SummerSlam. His match with CM Punk was disappointing, and The Viper returned to interfere.

While their feud has produced much better weekly segments this time around, the finish of their latest encounter still left much to be desired. Rhodes is spinning his wheels following another teased heel turn that didn't amount to anything new.

The American Nightmare has been in the same holding pattern for about two years, making it difficult to pinpoint who or what is responsible for his current decline.

Beneath Rhodes' carefully constructed public image, signs of frustration have grown apparent during some of his most recent interviews. After all, WWE has seemingly meddled in his last three WrestleMania storylines.

Sure, the company pivoted in response to the "We Want Cody" chants, and he successfully finished the story in 2024. However, John Cena's heel turn was a creative blunder the following year. This year, McAfee's involvement complicated a long-standing feud, which created an overproduced mess.

Even worse, WWE has a habit of reducing its best protagonists to gullible do-gooders, and it inevitably damages their credibility. Meanwhile, the villains retain their cool factor and outsmart them at every turn.

This creates a cycle where fans want to root for the bad guys, believing a heel turn is the only interesting character development. Roman Reigns and Cena went through the same thing because the company struggles to craft compelling material for its top faces.

On the surface, Rhodes is the pure babyface WWE has been searching for over the last decade. Presenting him as a gladhanding company man who won't take advantage of his opponent when they're down makes him unlikeable.

It's truly baffling that he continuously makes the same mistake in big matches when an old friend pleads with him. This cost him the match against Cena last year, but for some reason, the creative team keeps relying on this derivative finish.

At some point, there has to be a payoff to all these hints that he could cross the line. The Legend Killer is the perfect opponent to tell that story because it would finally give Rhodes the chance to surpass his mentor.

Still, it's reasonable to wonder how much of his current situation is self-imposed. Rhodes went through a similar rut towards the end of his run with AEW. Fans infamously called for a heel turn, and he refused.

The Rock also reportedly pitched a turn last year in the weeks leading up to his clash with Cena at The Showcase of the Immortals. Rhodes turned it down, but WWE was never fully on board with the pitch either, because he was a proven draw.

That raises the question of how much creative input he actually has. It's fair to reason that it wasn't the right time for him to break bad. Even though many viewers didn't want to boo him during his farewell tour, Cena was the more intriguing option.

Still, there was even a chance to do a double turn at SummerSlam. Similarly, longtime fans were nostalgic about Orton's heel persona, but he's not getting the heat that many expected. This was evident during their match in April.

Rhodes is still popular, but his character has grown stale. If he's not going to turn heel soon, he at least needs to show some edge. It's hard to root for someone who looks like he's being taken advantage of or overprotected.

It's a familiar narrative for a top star in WWE, but the company must find a compelling way to pay off months of teases. The American Nightmare was a revelation when no one else was set up to end Reigns' historic run, but the chase was more interesting.

That's largely because his storylines for the past two years were too repetitive, and his character has shown little development. The material was given, and situations involving McAfee and Travis Scott didn't help.

WWE has to take the lion's share of the blame for his current predicament. Even though the company handed him the ball during its hottest period in years, he proved himself to be a draw and a top merch seller.

Still, there was always this reluctance to fully invest in him as "the guy," especially when compared to the likes of The Rock, Cena, and Orton. To that end, it feels like Reigns never truly handed the mantle over to him, and Cody was just keeping his seat warm until he was ready to take it back.

Now, Rhodes is arguably the company's third-biggest star behind CM Punk, facing the choice of turning heel to right the ship. WWE must produce fresh matchups and stories for him soon to salvage this year.

articles.title: How can Oklahoma's newest additions help the defense?
articles.summary: How can the four newest Oklahoma Sooners have an impact on the defense this year?
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners have had a surprisingly busy stretch of roster movement over the last few weeks, with changes extending into the start of the regular season. However, general manager Jim Nagy and head coach Brent Venables feel they've done their jobs of making the team better throughout the process.

In addition to OU putting five walk-on players (wide receiver Trey Brown, offensive linemen Sean Hutton and Kenneth Wermy, defensive back Casen Calmus, and kicker Liam Evans) on scholarship before the season, the Sooners also saw CJ Nickson switch positions from defensive lineman to tight end .

However, most of the conversation has centered around the Sooners recently adding four new players to the roster via the new "five-for-five" ruling. Defensive linemen Danny Saili and Braxton Fely , linebacker Jaydon Southard , and defensive back D'Yoni Hill are the newest OU players. All four of the fifth-year players are now listed on the official roster heading into Oklahoma's game against Michigan on Saturday.

All four players were granted temporary restraining orders that allow them to play out a final season of eligibility with the Sooners, and none of the four players signed a pro contract. OU leadership was adamant they would not consider adding any players who had done so. Nagy assured that no players would be cut to make room for the four newcomers, and that OU was in constant contact with the SEC to make sure they followed the rules the whole way. Nagy also told the media on Monday that the Sooners didn't plan on adding any more players to the roster.

"We did everything by the book, so constant contact with the SEC, the administration," Nagy said. "We weren't going to cut any players, I'll say that. That was never a consideration, just looking to upgrade the team. It's a violent sport, it's a long season, and we are happy about what we did."

Saili, Fely, Southard, and Hill bring Oklahoma's total number of players on the roster to 114, but what will each of them add to their specific position groups, after coming in well after the normal time for roster additions in college football? Nagy and Venables know their job is to make OU's roster better, and they clearly saw areas where they felt the Sooners could use more depth. They left roster spots open in anticipation of the new ruling, and pursued players who they believed would be culture fits in the locker room. Once the new players are fully acclimated, they could become solid depth pieces at their respective positions.

Both Saili and Fely play defensive tackle, a position that OU lost a lot of production from after last season. In addition to losing Damonic Williams and Gracen Halton, the Sooners also saw Markus Strong, Siolaa Lolohea, and David Rowaiye walk out the door from last year's DT room.

Oklahoma has two strong starters in Jayden Jackson and David Stone, but Nagy and Venables wanted to add more depth alongside Bishop Thomas, Trent Wilson, Nigel Smith II, and James Carrington. Because so much of what the Sooners do defensively relies on strong interior d-line play, having good depth is pivotal. Pairing that with OU's strong defensive end room of Taylor Wein, Adepoju Adebawore, Danny Okoye, Wyatt Gilmore, Kenny Ozowalu, and Jake Kreul should make the Oklahoma front sturdy again this year.

Saili made his OU debut in Week 1 against UTEP, registering one tackle on seven snaps. He's got SEC experience from his two seasons at Arkansas, and Venables praised how well he's picked things up since he got to Norman in August. Fely spent four years at Boise State, and he was a three-year starter who made two all-conference teams. He has yet to see the field for the Sooners, after coming in much later than Saili, but he might be the player of the four that can help OU the most in 2026.

At linebacker, Oklahoma lost Kendal Daniels, Kobie McKinzie and Sammy Omosigho this offseason, so adding Southard is all about giving the depth at that position a boost in 2026. With Kip Lewis and Owen Heinecke as the two starters on the inside, Southard's presence gives the Sooners another veteran player in the middle of the defense.

Cole Sullivan, James Nesta, and Dane Bathurst are the other key linebackers on the depth chart in Norman, and this position's depth was also hurt by the spring ball injury to Taylor Heim. With Southard in the mix, Oklahoma has a player who developed into a star at FCS Stephen F. Austin and was first-team all-conference in 2025.

OU's Cheetah depth also gets a boost, as Sullivan and Nesta are the physically bigger options at that position that also includes starter Reggie Powers III and backups Jeremiah Newcombe and Lebron Bauer, all from the defensive back group. Having another linebacker frees up those players just a little bit more, and it allows Venables to have more versatility at the second level of his defense. Southard hasn't yet made his debut for OU, coming in after the UTEP game.

Hill plays cornerback, a position that saw OU lose Gentry Williams, Devon Jordan, Maliek Hawkins, and Kendel Dolby from the 2025 team. Hill's addition is all about adding more depth to the room, as the Sooners feel good about their starting duo of Eli Bowen and Courtland Guillory.

However, as much as the Sooners like the rest of their depth chart at CB with Jacobe Johnson, Trystan Haynes, and Dakoda Fields, bringing in a player like Hill, who has experience at the Power Four level, is a solid get for Oklahoma. He was a starter last year at Wisconsin, and with the way the Sooners like to rotate at cornerback, having a veteran player in the arsenal could prove to be big for the OU secondary, which also includes a strong safety group of Peyton Bowen, Michael Boganowski, Omarion Robinson, Markel Ford, Niko Jandreau, and Reed DeQuasie. Hill has also not yet made his OU debut, as he also came in after the UTEP game.

Eligibility in college football was a constant topic of the offseason, but with the class of 2022 players wanting to get in on the "five-for-five" rule, there was suddenly an opportunity for the Sooners to improve the roster. According to Nagy, he and Venables planned for this possibility, and Venables told the media that the Sooners heavily vetted each of the four players that they decided to bring in.

Once the opportunity presented itself, Oklahoma took advantage and made moves to improve the roster and add depth at key defensive positions. How much these four players contribute is yet to be seen, but Sooner Nation can rest assured that Nagy and Venables had a plan in place and were committed to using every legal avenue available to make Oklahoma better in 2026.

articles.title: Eggs, insults & a champion with a fake beard - Garcia and Benn face off
articles.summary: A performative Ryan Garcia shouted, repeatedly swore and taunted a composed Conor Benn with a boiled egg before Saturday's WBC welterweight title fight.
articles.body:
A performative Ryan Garcia shouted, repeatedly swore and even ate a boiled egg - while Briton Conor Benn kept his cool - during a peculiar news conference in Las Vegas.

American Garcia defends his WBC welterweight belt against 29-year-old Benn at the T-Mobile Arena on Saturday.

A fight week which had been relatively quiet finally came to life on Thursday - thanks largely to the unpredictable champion.

While Garcia, 28, bounced between insults, threats and jokes, Benn remained relatively composed.

Benn spoke instead about giving supporters "value for money" and refused to be drawn into many of his rival's taunts.

"All the talking, tweeting, typing and streaming is done - I'm ready to fight," Benn said, while inexplicably wearing a bullet-proof style vest.

Garcia is one of boxing's biggest social media stars, with more than 13 million Instagram followers.

He recently appeared on WWE's Monday Night Raw and it did not take long for the news conference to take on a similarly theatrical feel.

Minutes after taking his seat, Garcia reached into a bag, pulled out the egg, calmly peeled it and ate it whole.

"He has a lot of familiarity with eggs so I thought I'd eat some," Garcia said, as his opponent's father - Nigel Benn - shook his head.

It was a reference to Benn's two positive tests for clomifene in 2022 and the WBC's subsequent ruling that elevated consumption of eggs could provide a reasonable explanation.

Adding to the bizarre atmosphere, Garcia said his egg was a bit dry and would benefit from some honey.

Garcia has also served a doping suspension after testing positive for ostarine following his 2024 fight with Devin Haney. Both fighters have denied knowingly taking banned substances.

Before the face-off, security confiscated an egg Garcia had tucked into his pocket, potentially preventing a repeat of last year's incident when Chris Eubank Jr slapped Benn across the face with one.

Benn and Garcia had to be separated at their launch event in New York in July, but there was no repeat this time. As Garcia continued talking, Benn put a finger to his lips, smiled and eventually turned away and left the stage.

Thursday's news conference was held inside Saturday's fight venue, with one section of T-Mobile Arena curtained off for the crowd.

Fans had begun queuing more than an hour before the doors opened. It was not a Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez-sized crowd - and far from anything like the travelling support Ricky Hatton once brought to Las Vegas - but there was still a healthy turnout.

Small pockets of travelling British supporters made themselves heard, while Garcia received a much louder but mixed reception.

Garcia said Benn had "lit a fire" by questioning his Mexican heritage. Benn - who spent 12 years of his childhood living in Majorca - responded by speaking fluently in Spanish.

There was another dose of theatre when WBA 'Super' welterweight world champion Teofimo Lopez, disguised with a fake beard, stood among the crowd to ask a question before revealing himself to loud cheers.

Garcia also took aim at Benn's manager Keith Connolly's hairline before turning his attention to the challenger's weight.

Benn has not made the 10st 7lb welterweight limit for more than four years, having fought Chris Eubank Jr twice at middleweight.

Garcia suggested Benn could rehydrate to whatever weight he wanted after Friday's weigh-in but questioned whether his brain would recover sufficiently from the cut.

"[Garcia should] worry about himself," Benn replied. "He seems to have enough problems as it is.

"I don't look at him, I just worry about myself and don't cut corners. We'll see who makes weight tomorrow."

Garcia did eventually acknowledge much of the showmanship was just that.

"All this is noise, I've done my job and I'm the better fighter," he said. "This is fun but we know what to do."

But it did not take him long to slip back into entertainer mode. Even after Benn had left, Garcia remained on stage - flexing, shouting and playing to the crowd.
